title: Researchers Introduce QECLean Framework to Formally Verify Quantum Error-Correcting Codes in Lean 4 - Quantum Computing Report
gist: UW-Madison, University of Arizona and QEC Labs released QECLean, an open-source Lean 4 framework that machine-checks QEC code parameters, including the first exact distance-24 proof for IBM's [[360,12,24]] bivariate bicycle code and parametric proofs for infinite surface/color code families. It targets verification of AI-discovered codes where SAT/ILP solvers stall, though it verifies algebraic distance only, not circuit-level fault tolerance.

insights.claim: Computing the minimum distance of a quantum error-correcting code is NP-hard, and conventional integer linear programming and SAT solvers typically stall on codes with distances above 18 and cannot certify infinite code families.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: As codes grow, claimed parameters of new qLDPC codes become hard to trust without formal methods, creating a need for verification tooling.
insights.quote: typically stall on codes with distances above 18
insights.locator: Because computing minimum code distance is NP-hard

insights.claim: QECLean is aimed at the growing challenge of verifying complex, algorithmically discovered QEC codes, and is designed to validate AI-discovered codes and future verified quantum compilers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: AI-driven code discovery creates a parallel need for proof infrastructure; formal verification may become a standard gate for new QEC codes.
insights.locator: the library addresses the growing challenge

insights.claim: QECLean, built on the Lean 4 proof assistant by researchers from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, the University of Arizona and QEC Labs, is an open-source framework that mechanically proves the parameters of quantum error-correcting codes.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Open-source formal tooling lowers the cost for hardware firms to certify their chosen codes.
insights.locator: Researchers from the University of Wisconsin-Madison

insights.claim: QECLean links stabilizer groups, binary symplectic check matrices, and homological chain complexes inside Lean's dependent type system, so a code is specified once and each property is proved in its most tractable representation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A multi-representation approach is what makes large-code proofs feasible; a reusable pattern for verification tools.
insights.locator: QECLean bridges this gap by linking

insights.claim: Stavan Jain, Nithin Raveendran and Aws Albarghouthi developed compositional code combinators for QECLean, including a generalized double-cover combinator that derives the distance of a 2n-qubit lifted code from an n-qubit base code, enabling verification of large qLDPC codes.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Compositional proofs let verification scale with qLDPC architectures favored by IBM and others.
insights.locator: To scale verification to large quantum low-density

insights.claim: QECLean comprises roughly 57,000 lines of Lean code and 312,000 lines of kernel-checked certificates.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Substantial engineering investment indicates a durable library rather than a one-off proof.

insights.claim: QECLean proved the exact distance of IBM's 360-qubit bivariate bicycle code [[360, 12, 24]] to be 24, which was previously known only as an upper bound.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Independently confirms the error-correction capability of a code in IBM's qLDPC roadmap family.

insights.claim: QECLean verified IBM's [[144, 12, 12]] Gross code as a double cover of a [[72, 12, 6]] base code, and verified Oratomic's high-rate (1/5) [[150, 30, 10]] Mitten non-abelian lifted-product code.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Formal certification of vendor codes (IBM, Oratomic) adds credibility to their QEC overhead claims.

insights.claim: QECLean delivered the first machine-checked parametric distance proof across an infinite planar code family, the rotated surface codes [[L², 1, L]] for odd L ≥ 3, and also parametrically verified toric and triangular color code families.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Proofs over whole families, not single instances, are a capability solvers cannot provide.

insights.claim: QECLean's current release verifies algebraic code distance only, not physical circuit-level fault tolerance or noise thresholds.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A verified code distance does not guarantee hardware-level performance; circuit-level claims still need separate scrutiny.
